dispositions.rationale: The existing suite is the agy launcher's whole behavioural contract, one case per criterion of its own spec, including its stderr ledger in both modes. Passing it unchanged, with only the model argument rewritten, is the observation that nothing outside the model element changed. A stderr line on a path that suite does not exercise is a path the launcher's contract does not define, and no document obligation reaches it.

DEL-A1 states its obligation for any Markdown file the lint reads and checks a nested file three directories down. A lint that skips an existing file violates DEL-A1 as stated, and DEL-A2 then observes the landed tree through that same lint. The objection needs an implementation that reads the fixtures and not the tree, which DEL-A2's reported file list exposes.

This spec's slices state the Kimi constraint once, in the OpenRouter skill, and DEL-C7 confines slice C's diff to the named passages. A second copy in another skill would be a later change outside this document, and DEL-D1's lint refuses the form such a copy takes when it restates the model row.

No slice changes a worker instruction. DEL-C7 holds every file slice C touches unchanged outside the named passages, so the worker text that exists today survives as it is, and a wrong worker instruction would be a defect of today's skill, not of this change.

The obligation is that a reader gives the right response to each signal, which DEL-C3 checks. Whether harvest.md presents the mapping as a table is its form, and a mapping in prose that passes every scenario fails no promised outcome.

The existing suite includes the watchdog, signal and timeout cases of the launcher's own spec, and DEL-G4 requires it to pass unchanged. A watchdog bypass on a path that suite does not exercise is a path the launcher's contract does not define.

Promotion before implementation is a tracker step the work facade enforces on the items section 7 lists. It is an instruction to whoever opens those items, and no acceptance check of the delivered change can observe it.

Landing order is stated in section 7 and is held by dependency edges between the work items. A check of the combined tree cannot observe the order two changes landed in, so no criterion of the change can carry it.

The existing suite is the launcher's behavioural contract, and DEL-G4 names the one edit allowed to it. A further assertion added to the suite is a change to the check, which the criterion forbids, not a way to pass it.
